messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We're building backend for a helpdesk SaaS for businesses and their customers.
Use Rails in API-only mode; the frontend is a separate app.
Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL are installed. If you need anything else, install it yourself.
Use `DATABASE_URL`. Work in `/app`.

Let's start with business signup. An owner should be able to register their business, verify their
email, sign in, update their name, change their password, and recover a forgotten password. Each
business has its own users; the same email can belong to different businesses.

Use JSON under `/api/v1`. Signup should look like this:

```http
POST /api/v1/account/create
Content-Type: application/json

{"account":{"name":"Acme","subdomain":"acme","admin":{"name":"Jo","email":"jo@acme.test","password":"my-first-password"}}}
```

Return the new `account` and `user`. Jo is an admin, but needs to verify their email before signing
in. Include record IDs, timestamps, and the user's `role` and `verified` flag.
Use `X-Helpdesk-Account: acme` to choose the business on subsequent requests. Public `GET /portal`
returns its name and subdomain inside `portal`; signed-in users get the full account at `GET /account`.

For login, accept `POST /sessions` with `{"session":{"email":"jo@acme.test","password":"my-first-password"}}`.
Return the user and account alongside `session.token`, which clients send as `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN`.
`DELETE /session` signs out that session. Use `GET /me` and `PATCH /me` for the user's profile, with
changes such as `{"user":{"name":"Jo Smith"}}`. Password changes go to `PUT /me/password` as
`{"password_change":{"current_password":"my-first-password","password":"my-new-password"}}`.

Send verification and password-reset links to the frontend at `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL`, default
`http://localhost:3001`. Use `/verify-email?account=acme&token=TOKEN` and
`/reset-password?account=acme&token=TOKEN`. The frontend submits the token to
`POST /email_verifications/confirm` as `{"email_verification":{"token":"TOKEN"}}`, or to
`POST /password_resets/confirm` as `{"password_reset":{"token":"TOKEN","password":"my-new-password"}}`.
Users can request another link through `POST /email_verifications` or `POST /password_resets`,
using the same envelopes with an `email` instead. New links replace old ones.
Changing a password should sign out existing sessions.
Allow requests from the configured frontend origin.

Send outgoing email using Action Mailer. Use `HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM` for the sender,
defaulting to `support@example.test`.

Let the owner cancel the account with `POST /account/cancel` and reactivate it with
`POST /account/reactivate` within 90 days. Cancellation revokes sessions and stops ordinary
business access. The owner can still sign in to reactivate the account. Permanently delete
accounts still cancelled after 90 days, including all their data.
Provide `bin/rails helpdesk:purge_cancelled_accounts` for this cleanup.


You can execute bash commands and edit files to implement the necessary changes.

That confirms it: `password=` silently ignores `""`. A blank password in a change or reset request would "succeed" without changing anything, so I'll reject blank assignments explicitly in the model.

cd /app && cat > config/database.yml <<'EOF'
# PostgreSQL. The connection comes from DATABASE_URL: Rails merges it over the
# settings below for the current environment. The database names here are only
# fallbacks for when DATABASE_URL is not set.
#
# config/environments/test.rb moves the test environment onto a separate "_test"
# database so that the test suite never touches the development data.
default: &default
  adapter: postgresql
  encoding: unicode
  pool: <%= ENV.fetch("RAILS_MAX_THREADS", 5) %>

development:
  <<: *default
  database: helpdesk_development

test:
  <<: *default
  database: helpdesk_test

production:
  <<: *default
  database: helpdesk_production
EOF
cat > config/environments/test.rb <<'EOF'
require "active_support/core_ext/integer/time"

# DATABASE_URL names the development database and Rails merges it over
# database.yml, so the test environment must point it somewhere else. Use
# TEST_DATABASE_URL if given, otherwise the same database name with "_test".
if ENV["TEST_DATABASE_URL"].present?
  ENV["DATABASE_URL"] = ENV["TEST_DATABASE_URL"]
elsif ENV["DATABASE_URL"].present?
  uri = URI.parse(ENV["DATABASE_URL"])
  name = uri.path.delete_prefix("/").sub(/_(development|production)\z/, "")
  name += "_test" unless name.end_with?("_test")
  uri.path = "/#{name}"
  ENV["DATABASE_URL"] = uri.to_s
end

Rails.application.configure do
  # Settings specified here will take precedence over those in config/application.rb.

  # While tests run files are not watched, reloading is not necessary.
  config.enable_reloading = false

  # Eager loading loads your entire application. When running a single test locally,
  # this is usually not necessary, and can slow down your test suite. However, it's
  # recommended that you enable it in continuous integration systems to ensure eager
  # loading is working properly before deploying your code.
  config.eager_load = ENV["CI"].present?

  # Configure public file server for tests with cache-control for performance.
  config.public_file_server.headers = { "cache-control" => "public, max-age=3600" }

  # Show full error reports.
  config.consider_all_requests_local = true
  config.cache_store = :null_store

  # Render exception templates for rescuable exceptions and raise for other exceptions.
  config.action_dispatch.show_exceptions = :rescuable

  # Disable request forgery protection in test environment.
  config.action_controller.allow_forgery_protection = false

  # Store uploaded files on the local file system in a temporary directory.
  # Tell Action Mailer not to deliver emails to the real world.
  # The :test delivery method accumulates sent emails in the
  # ActionMailer::Base.deliveries array.
  config.action_mailer.delivery_method = :test

  # Print deprecation notices to the stderr.
  config.active_support.deprecation = :stderr

  # Raise error when a before_action's only/except options reference missing actions
  config.action_controller.raise_on_missing_callback_actions = true
end
EOF
cat > config/initializers/helpdesk.rb <<'EOF'
module Helpdesk
  # Runtime settings, read from the environment when used so that changing the
  # environment (for example in tests) takes effect without restarting.
  module Settings
    DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL = "http://localhost:3001".freeze
    DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM = "support@example.test".freeze

    class << self
      # Base URL of the separately hosted frontend, without a trailing slash.
      def frontend_url
        (ENV["HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL"].presence || DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL).delete_suffix("/")
      end

      # Scheme, host and port only. This is the value browsers send as the Origin header.
      def frontend_origin
        uri = URI.parse(frontend_url)
        port = uri.port == uri.default_port ? "" : ":#{uri.port}"
        "#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}#{port}"
      end

      # Link the frontend turns into a request, e.g. /verify-email?account=acme&token=...
      def frontend_link(path, account:, token:)
        "#{frontend_url}#{path}?#{{ account: account, token: token }.to_query}"
      end

      def mail_from
        ENV["HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM"].presence || DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM
      end
    end
  end
end
EOF
cat > config/initializers/cors.rb <<'EOF'
# Lets the separately hosted frontend call the API from the browser.
# Only the configured frontend origin is allowed (HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL).
Rails.application.config.middleware.insert_before 0, Rack::Cors do
  allow do
    origins Helpdesk::Settings.frontend_origin

    resource "/api/*",
      headers: %w[Authorization Content-Type Accept X-Helpdesk-Account],
      methods: %i[get post put patch delete options head],
      max_age: 600
  end
end
EOF

messages.content: Next I'll set the mailer delivery config per environment, then do the Action Mailer, model, and migration work. I'm using `:file` delivery in development so emails land in `tmp/mails`, and SMTP settings from ENV in production.

arguments.command:
cd /app && python3 - <<'PY'
import re
p='config/environments/development.rb'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('  config.action_mailer.default_url_options = { host: "localhost", port: 3000 }\n',
'''  # Write outgoing mail to tmp/mails instead of sending it.
  config.action_mailer.delivery_method = :file
''')
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='config/environments/production.rb'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('  config.action_mailer.default_url_options = { host: "example.com" }\n',
'''  # Outgoing mail goes through SMTP; configure it with environment variables.
  config.action_mailer.delivery_method = :smtp
  config.action_mailer.raise_delivery_errors = true
  smtp_settings = {
    address: ENV.fetch("SMTP_ADDRESS", "localhost"),
    port: ENV.fetch("SMTP_PORT", 587).to_i,
    domain: ENV["SMTP_DOMAIN"],
    user_name: ENV["SMTP_USERNAME"],
    password: ENV["SMTP_PASSWORD"],
    authentication: (:plain if ENV["SMTP_USERNAME"].present?),
    enable_starttls_auto: true
  }
  config.action_mailer.smtp_settings = smtp_settings.compact
''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
grep -n "action_mailer" config/environments/*.rb; echo; cat > app/mailers/application_mailer.rb <<'EOF'
class ApplicationMailer < ActionMailer::Base
  # A proc, so HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM is read when mail is sent, not at boot.
  default from: proc { Helpdesk::Settings.mail_from }
  layout "mailer"
end
EOF

require_relative "../config/environment"

EOF

# A business using the helpdesk. Everything else belongs to exactly one account.
class Account < ApplicationRecord
  # Cancelled accounts can be reactivated for this long, then purged for good.
  REACTIVATION_WINDOW = 90.days

  SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT = /\A[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])\z/
  RESERVED_SUBDOMAINS = %w[admin api app assets mail smtp static status www].freeze

  has_many :users, dependent: :destroy

  normalizes :name, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }
  normalizes :subdomain, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :name, presence: true, length: { maximum: 120 }
  validates :subdomain,
            presence: true,
            uniqueness: true,
            format: { with: SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT, message: "may only use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens" },
            exclusion: { in: RESERVED_SUBDOMAINS, message: "is reserved" }

  scope :cancelled_before, ->(time) { where(cancelled_at: ..time) }

  def cancelled?
    cancelled_at.present?
  end

  def reactivation_deadline
    cancelled_at && (cancelled_at + REACTIVATION_WINDOW)
  end

  def reactivation_open?(now = Time.current)
    cancelled? && now < reactivation_deadline
  end

  # Cancelling stops ordinary access and signs every user out. The data is kept
  # until the reactivation window closes.
  def cancel!(now: Time.current)
    transaction do
      update!(cancelled_at: now)
      Session.where(user_id: users.select(:id)).delete_all
    end
  end

  def reactivate!
    update!(cancelled_at: nil)
  end

  # Permanently deletes accounts cancelled more than REACTIVATION_WINDOW ago,
  # along with all their users, sessions and tokens. Returns the number purged.
  def self.purge_cancelled!(now: Time.current)
    cutoff = now - REACTIVATION_WINDOW
    purged = 0

    cancelled_before(cutoff).ids.each do |id|
      transaction do
        # Re-check under a row lock: the account may have been reactivated since the query.
        account = lock.find_by(id: id)
        next unless account&.cancelled_at && account.cancelled_at <= cutoff

        account.destroy!
        purged += 1
      end
    end

    purged
  end

  def as_api_json
    {
      id: id,
      name: name,
      subdomain: subdomain,
      status: cancelled? ? "cancelled" : "active",
      cancelled_at: cancelled_at,
      reactivation_deadline: reactivation_deadline,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end
end
EOF

# A signed-in device. The client holds the raw token; only its digest is stored.
class Session < ApplicationRecord
  TTL = 30.days

  belongs_to :user

  validates :token_digest, :expires_at, presence: true

  # Returns [session, raw_token]. The raw token is shown once, at sign-in.
  def self.issue!(user)
    raw = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
    session = user.sessions.create!(token_digest: digest(raw), expires_at: TTL.from_now)
    [session, raw]
  end

  def self.find_active(raw)
    return nil if raw.blank?

    where("expires_at > ?", Time.current).find_by(token_digest: digest(raw))
  end

  def self.digest(raw)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw.to_s)
  end
end

# Emailed tokens (email verification, password reset). Each user has at most one
# live token of each kind. Issuing a new one replaces the old, and redeeming a
# token deletes it, so it works once.
module SingleUseToken
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  # Raised when a token is unknown, expired, already used, or for another business.
  class InvalidToken < StandardError; end

  included do
    belongs_to :user

    validates :token_digest, :expires_at, presence: true
  end

  class_methods do
    # Returns the raw token to email. Only its digest is stored.
    def issue!(user)
      raw = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
      user.with_lock do
        where(user_id: user.id).delete_all
        create!(user: user, token_digest: digest(raw), expires_at: self::TTL.from_now)
      end
      raw
    end

    # Deletes and returns the matching token record, or raises InvalidToken.
    # Call inside a transaction, so a later failure also gives the token back.
    def redeem!(raw, account: nil)
      scope = where(token_digest: digest(raw))
      scope = scope.where(user_id: account.users.select(:id)) if account

      record = scope.lock.first
      raise InvalidToken unless record&.expires_at&.future?

      record.destroy!
      record
    end

    def digest(raw)
      Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw.to_s)
    end
  end
end
EOF

# Every error response has the same shape:
#   {"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "errors": {...}}}
# where "errors" is present only for validation failures.
module ErrorHandling
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    rescue_from ActionController::ParameterMissing, with: :render_parameter_missing
    rescue_from ActionDispatch::Http::Parameters::ParseError, with: :render_bad_json
    rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, with: :render_record_invalid
    rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, with: :render_record_not_unique
    rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound, with: :render_record_not_found
  end

  private

  def render_error(status, code, message, errors: nil)
    body = { code: code, message: message }
    body[:errors] = errors if errors.present?
    render json: { error: body }, status: status
  end

  def render_validation_failed(errors)
    render_error(:unprocessable_entity, "validation_failed", "Some fields are invalid.", errors: errors)
  end

  def render_parameter_missing(exception)
    render_error(:bad_request, "parameter_missing", exception.message)
  end

  def render_bad_json(_exception)
    render_error(:bad_request, "invalid_json", "The request body is not valid JSON.")
  end

  def render_record_invalid(exception)
    render_validation_failed(exception.record.errors.to_hash)
  end

  def render_record_not_unique(_exception)
    render_error(:conflict, "conflict", "That record was created by another request. Please try again.")
  end

  def render_record_not_found(_exception)
    render_error(:not_found, "not_found", "The requested record was not found.")
  end
end

# Chooses the business for a request from the X-Helpdesk-Account header.
module AccountScoped
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  ACCOUNT_HEADER = "X-Helpdesk-Account".freeze

  private

  def requested_subdomain
    request.headers[ACCOUNT_HEADER].to_s.strip.downcase.presence
  end

  # The business named by the header, or nil if no header was sent. If the
  # header names an unknown business, this renders 404 and the caller must stop
  # (check `performed?`).
  def optional_account_from_header
    return nil if requested_subdomain.nil?

    account = Account.find_by(subdomain: requested_subdomain)
    render_error(:not_found, "account_not_found", "No business matches the X-Helpdesk-Account header.") unless account
    account
  end

  # Like optional_account_from_header, but the header is required. Renders 400
  # when it is missing.
  def account_from_header!
    if requested_subdomain.nil?
      render_error(:bad_request, "account_header_required", "Send the X-Helpdesk-Account header to choose a business.")
      return nil
    end

    optional_account_from_header
  end
end
EOF

# Bearer-token sessions. Callers include `before_action :authenticate_session!`.
#
# A cancelled account blocks everything except the actions listed with
# `available_while_cancelled`, which the owner needs to reactivate the account.
module Authenticatable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    class_attribute :cancelled_account_actions, instance_writer: false, default: [].freeze
  end

  class_methods do
    def available_while_cancelled(*actions)
      self.cancelled_account_actions = (cancelled_account_actions + actions.map(&:to_s)).freeze
    end
  end

  private

  attr_reader :current_session, :current_user, :current_account

  def authenticate_session!
    session = Session.find_active(bearer_token)
    return render_error(:unauthorized, "unauthenticated", "Sign in to continue.") unless session

    user = session.user
    account = user.account

    if requested_subdomain && requested_subdomain != account.subdomain
      return render_error(:forbidden, "account_mismatch", "This session belongs to a different business.")
    end

    @current_session = session
    @current_user = user
    @current_account = account

    return if !account.cancelled? || self.class.cancelled_account_actions.include?(action_name)

    render_error(:forbidden, "account_cancelled", "This business has been cancelled.")
  end

  def require_account_owner!
    return if current_user.admin?

    render_error(:forbidden, "owner_only", "Only the account owner can do that.")
  end

  def bearer_token
    request.authorization.to_s[/\ABearer\s+(\S+)\z/i, 1]
  end
end
EOF

module Api
  module V1
    class AccountsController < ApplicationController
      before_action :authenticate_session!, only: %i[show cancel reactivate]
      before_action :require_account_owner!, only: %i[cancel reactivate]

      available_while_cancelled :show, :reactivate

      # Sign up a business. The admin must verify their email before signing in.
      def create
        input = params.require(:account).permit(:name, :subdomain, admin: %i[name email password])
        admin_input = input[:admin] || {}

        account = Account.new(name: input[:name], subdomain: input[:subdomain])
        admin = User.new(
          account: account,
          role: "admin",
          name: admin_input[:name],
          email: admin_input[:email],
          password: admin_input[:password]
        )

        # Validate both before saving, so the response reports every problem at once.
        account_valid = account.valid?
        admin_valid = admin.valid?
        unless account_valid && admin_valid
          errors = account.errors.to_hash.transform_keys { |key| "account.#{key}" }
                          .merge(admin.errors.to_hash.transform_keys { |key| "admin.#{key}" })
          return render_validation_failed(errors)
        end

        verification_token = nil
        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          admin.save!
          verification_token = EmailVerification.issue!(admin)
        end
        UserMailer.deliver_safely(:email_verification, admin, verification_token)

        render json: { account: account.as_api_json, user: admin.as_api_json }, status: :created
      end

      def show
        render json: { account: current_account.as_api_json }
      end

      def cancel
        current_account.cancel!
        render json: { account: current_account.as_api_json }
      end

      def reactivate
        return render_error(:unprocessable_entity, "not_cancelled", "This business is not cancelled.") unless current_account.cancelled?

        unless current_account.reactivation_open?
          return render_error(
            :unprocessable_entity,
            "reactivation_window_closed",
            "Cancelled businesses can only be reactivated within #{Account::REACTIVATION_WINDOW.inspect} of cancellation."
          )
        end

        current_account.reactivate!
        render json: { account: current_account.as_api_json }
      end
    end
  end
end
EOF

module Api
  module V1
    class SessionsController < ApplicationController
      before_action :authenticate_session!, only: :destroy

      available_while_cancelled :destroy

      # Sign in. With X-Helpdesk-Account, the email is looked up in that business.
      # Without it, the email must belong to exactly one business.
      def create
        credentials = params.require(:session).permit(:email, :password)
        password = credentials[:password].to_s

        account = optional_account_from_header
        return if performed?

        candidates = (account ? account.users : User.all).where(email: credentials[:email]).includes(:account).to_a
        matches = candidates.select { |user| user.authenticate(password) }

        if matches.empty?
          # Hash anyway when no user matched, so response time does not reveal whether the email exists.
          BCrypt::Password.create(password) if candidates.empty?
          return render_error(:unauthorized, "invalid_credentials", "Email or password is incorrect.")
        end

        if matches.many?
          return render_error(
            :unprocessable_entity,
            "account_required",
            "This email belongs to several businesses. Send the X-Helpdesk-Account header to choose one."
          )
        end

        user = matches.first
        return render_error(:forbidden, "email_not_verified", "Verify your email address before signing in.") unless user.verified?

        if user.account.cancelled? && !user.admin?
          return render_error(:forbidden, "account_cancelled", "This business has been cancelled.")
        end

        session, token = Session.issue!(user)
        render json: {
          session: { token: token, expires_at: session.expires_at },
          user: user.as_api_json,
          account: user.account.as_api_json
        }, status: :created
      end

      def destroy
        current_session.destroy!
        head :no_content
      end
    end
  end
end
EOF

module Api
  module V1
    # Changes the signed-in user's password. This signs out every session, including this one.
    class PasswordsController < ApplicationController
      before_action :authenticate_session!

      available_while_cancelled :update

      def update
        change = params.require(:password_change).permit(:current_password, :password)

        unless current_user.authenticate(change[:current_password].to_s)
          return render_error(
            :unprocessable_entity,
            "invalid_current_password",
            "The current password is incorrect.",
            errors: { current_password: [ "is incorrect" ] }
          )
        end

        User.transaction do
          current_user.update!(password: change[:password])
          current_user.sessions.delete_all
        end

        render json: {
          message: "Password changed. All sessions were signed out, so sign in again.",
          user: current_user.as_api_json
        }
      end
    end
  end
end

module Api
  module V1
    class EmailVerificationsController < ApplicationController
      GENERIC_MESSAGE = "If that email belongs to an account that needs verifying, a verification link is on its way.".freeze

      # Sends a fresh verification link. Replaces any earlier link.
      def create
        account = optional_account_from_header
        return if performed?

        email = params.require(:email_verification).permit(:email)[:email]
        scope = (account ? account.users : User.all).where(email: email, verified_at: nil)

        scope.includes(:account).each do |user|
          token = EmailVerification.issue!(user)
          UserMailer.deliver_safely(:email_verification, user, token)
        end

        render json: { message: GENERIC_MESSAGE }, status: :accepted
      end

      def confirm
        account = optional_account_from_header
        return if performed?

        token = params.require(:email_verification).permit(:token)[:token]
        user = nil

        EmailVerification.transaction do
          record = EmailVerification.redeem!(token, account: account)
          user = record.user
          user.verified_at ||= Time.current
          user.save!
        end

        render json: { message: "Email verified. You can sign in now.", user: user.as_api_json, account: user.account.as_api_json }
      rescue SingleUseToken::InvalidToken
        render_invalid_token
      end

      private

      def render_invalid_token
        render_error(:unprocessable_entity, "invalid_token", "This link is invalid or has expired. Request a new one.")
      end
    end
  end
end

module Api
  module V1
    class PasswordResetsController < ApplicationController
      GENERIC_MESSAGE = "If that email belongs to an account, a password reset link is on its way.".freeze

      # Sends a fresh reset link. Replaces any earlier link.
      def create
        account = optional_account_from_header
        return if performed?

        email = params.require(:password_reset).permit(:email)[:email]
        scope = account ? account.users : User.all

        scope.where(email: email).includes(:account).each do |user|
          token = PasswordReset.issue!(user)
          UserMailer.deliver_safely(:password_reset, user, token)
        end

        render json: { message: GENERIC_MESSAGE }, status: :accepted
      end

      def confirm
        account = optional_account_from_header
        return if performed?

        input = params.require(:password_reset).permit(:token, :password)
        user = nil

        PasswordReset.transaction do
          record = PasswordReset.redeem!(input[:token], account: account)
          user = record.user
          user.password = input[:password]
          # Following the reset link proves the user controls the mailbox.
          user.verified_at ||= Time.current
          user.save!
          user.sessions.delete_all
        end

        render json: {
          message: "Password reset. Sign in with your new password.",
          user: user.as_api_json
        }
      rescue SingleUseToken::InvalidToken
        render_error(:unprocessable_entity, "invalid_token", "This link is invalid or has expired. Request a new one.")
      end
    end
  end
end

messages.content: The app was right and my script was wrong. Rails' `:file` delivery appends every mail for a recipient to one file, and my helper took the *first* token in the file, which is the verification link. I'll re-run the reset checks using the last token, and fix the sign-in step that depended on it.

arguments.command:
cat > /tmp/smoke3.sh <<'EOF'
B=http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1
J='Content-Type: application/json'
H='X-Helpdesk-Account: acme'
req() { curl -s -w '\n[%{http_code}]\n' "$@"; }
tok() { python3 -c 'import sys,json; d=sys.stdin.read().rsplit("\n[",1)[0]; print(json.loads(d)["session"]["token"])'; }
# :file delivery appends all mail for a recipient to one file: take the most recent token.
last_token() { grep -o 'token=[^ \r]*' /app/tmp/mails/jo@acme.test | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2 | tr -d '\r\n'; }

echo "=== reset link #1 requested"
req -X POST $B/password_resets -H "$J" -H "$H" -d '{"password_reset":{"email":"jo@acme.test"}}' >/dev/null
RESET1=$(last_token)
echo "=== reset link #2 requested (replaces #1)"
req -X POST $B/password_resets -H "$J" -H "$H" -d '{"password_reset":{"email":"jo@acme.test"}}' >/dev/null
RESET2=$(last_token)
echo "reset1=$RESET1"; echo "reset2=$RESET2"
echo "=== link #1 (expect 422, replaced)"
req -X POST $B/password_resets/confirm -H "$J" -H "$H" -d "{\"password_reset\":{\"token\":\"$RESET1\",\"password\":\"another-password\"}}"
echo "=== link #2 with too-short password (expect 422, link kept)"
req -X POST $B/password_resets/confirm -H "$J" -H "$H" -d "{\"password_reset\":{\"token\":\"$RESET2\",\"password\":\"x\"}}"
echo "=== link #2 with blank password (expect 422, link kept)"
req -X POST $B/password_resets/confirm -H "$J" -H "$H" -d "{\"password_reset\":{\"token\":\"$RESET2\",\"password\":\"\"}}"
echo "=== link #2 valid (expect 200)"
req -X POST $B/password_resets/confirm -H "$J" -H "$H" -d "{\"password_reset\":{\"token\":\"$RESET2\",\"password\":\"reset-password-1\"}}"
echo "=== link #2 reuse (expect 422)"
req -X POST $B/password_resets/confirm -H "$J" -H "$H" -d "{\"password_reset\":{\"token\":\"$RESET2\",\"password\":\"reset-password-2\"}}"
echo "=== sign in with reset password (expect 201)"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '[%{http_code}]\n' -X POST $B/sessions -H "$J" -H "$H" -d '{"session":{"email":"jo@acme.test","password":"reset-password-1"}}'
echo "=== old password (expect 401)"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '[%{http_code}]\n' -X POST $B/sessions -H "$J" -H "$H" -d '{"session":{"email":"jo@acme.test","password":"my-new-password"}}'

echo "=== email verification resend for verified user (expect 202, no mail)"
BEFORE=$(grep -c 'Subject:' /app/tmp/mails/jo@acme.test)
req -X POST $B/email_verifications -H "$J" -H "$H" -d '{"email_verification":{"email":"jo@acme.test"}}'
AFTER=$(grep -c 'Subject:' /app/tmp/mails/jo@acme.test); echo "mails before=$BEFORE after=$AFTER"

echo "=== sign in without header (email unique across businesses) (expect 201)"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '[%{http_code}]\n' -X POST $B/sessions -H "$J" -d '{"session":{"email":"jo@acme.test","password":"reset-password-1"}}'
echo "=== sign in with unknown header (expect 404)"
curl -s -w '\n[%{http_code}]\n' -X POST $B/sessions -H "$J" -H "X-Helpdesk-Account: nope" -d '{"session":{"email":"jo@acme.test","password":"reset-password-1"}}'
echo "=== sign in with wrong password (expect 401)"
curl -s -w '\n[%{http_code}]\n' -X POST $B/sessions -H "$J" -H "$H" -d '{"session":{"email":"jo@acme.test","password":"nope-nope-nope"}}'
echo "=== malformed JSON (expect 400)"
curl -s -w '\n[%{http_code}]\n' -X POST $B/sessions -H "$J" -d '{"session":'
echo "=== missing body envelope (expect 400)"
curl -s -w '\n[%{http_code}]\n' -X POST $B/sessions -H "$J" -H "$H" -d '{"email":"x"}'
EOF
bash /tmp/smoke3.sh

messages.content: Two of my script's bugs showed up. The `[^ \r]` pattern in `grep` excludes a literal `r` character, which cut off any token containing one (or starting with one). Also, the reset-link checks ran against the wrong token. I'll switch to a proper whitespace match and re-run the reset checks.

arguments.command:
cat > /tmp/lib.sh <<'EOF'
B=http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1
J='Content-Type: application/json'
H='X-Helpdesk-Account: acme'
req() { curl -s -w '\n[%{http_code}]\n' "$@"; }
# Latest token from the file-delivery mailbox for an address.
last_token() { python3 - "$1" <<'PY'
import re,sys
data=open(f"/app/tmp/mails/{sys.argv[1]}").read()
print(re.findall(r"token=(\S+)", data)[-1].strip())
PY
}
EOF
cat > /tmp/smoke4.sh <<'EOF'

echo "=== reset link #1"
req -X POST $B/password_resets -H "$J" -H "$H" -d '{"password_reset":{"email":"jo@acme.test"}}' >/dev/null

echo "=== reset link #2 (replaces #1)"
req -X POST $B/password_resets -H "$J" -H "$H" -d '{"password_reset":{"email":"jo@acme.test"}}' >/dev/null
RESET2=$(last_token jo@acme.test)

messages.content: All reset behaviors now check out. Replacing a link invalidates the old one, bad passwords keep the link usable, a good reset works once, and the new password signs in. Next is the cancel and reactivate lifecycle. I'll run it against the live server and add a non-owner agent through the console, since no API creates agents yet.

# Shared helpers for the JSON API integration tests.
module ApiHelpers
  include ActiveSupport::Testing::TimeHelpers

  PASSWORD = "my-first-password".freeze
  NEW_PASSWORD = "my-new-password".freeze
  FRONTEND_URL = "http://localhost:3001".freeze

  def api(method, path, body: nil, token: nil, account: nil, headers: {})
    request_headers = { "Accept" => "application/json" }.merge(headers)
    request_headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer #{token}" if token
    request_headers["X-Helpdesk-Account"] = account if account

    if body.nil?
      send(method, "/api/v1#{path}", headers: request_headers)
    else
      request_headers["CONTENT_TYPE"] = "application/json"
      send(method, "/api/v1#{path}", params: body.to_json, headers: request_headers)
    end
  end

  def api_get(path, **options) = api(:get, path, **options)
  def api_post(path, body = nil, **options) = api(:post, path, body: body, **options)
  def api_patch(path, body, **options) = api(:patch, path, body: body, **options)
  def api_put(path, body, **options) = api(:put, path, body: body, **options)
  def api_delete(path, **options) = api(:delete, path, **options)

  def json
    JSON.parse(response.body)
  end

  def signup!(subdomain: "acme", name: "Acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: PASSWORD)
    api_post("/account/create", {
      account: {
        name: name,
        subdomain: subdomain,
        admin: { name: "Jo", email: email, password: password }
      }
    })
  end

  # The most recent mail sent to an address whose subject contains the fragment.
  def latest_mail(to:, subject:)
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.reverse.find do |mail|
      Array(mail.to).include?(to) && mail.subject.include?(subject)
    end
  end

  def token_from_latest_mail(to:, subject:)
    mail = latest_mail(to: to, subject: subject)
    assert mail, "expected an email to #{to} with subject containing #{subject.inspect}"
    mail.body.decoded[/token=(\S+)/, 1]
  end

  def verification_token(email, account: "acme")
    token_from_latest_mail(to: email, subject: "Verify your email for")
  end

  def reset_token(email)
    token_from_latest_mail(to: email, subject: "Reset your password")
  end

  def verify_email!(email, account: "acme")
    api_post("/email_verifications/confirm", { email_verification: { token: verification_token(email) } }, account: account)
  end

  # Verifies the owner's email and signs them in. Returns the session token.
  def verified_sign_in!(email: "jo@acme.test", password: PASSWORD, account: "acme")
    verify_email!(email, account: account)
    assert_response :ok
    sign_in!(email: email, password: password, account: account)
  end

  def sign_in!(email:, password: PASSWORD, account: "acme")
    api_post("/sessions", { session: { email: email, password: password } }, account: account)
    assert_response :created, "sign-in failed: #{response.body}"
    json.dig("session", "token")
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class AccountLifecycleTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    signup!
    @owner_token = verified_sign_in!
    @agent = User.create!(
      account: Account.find_by!(subdomain: "acme"),
      name: "Ann",
      email: "ann@acme.test",
      password: "agent-password",
      role: "agent",
      verified_at: Time.current
    )
    @agent_token = sign_in!(email: "ann@acme.test", password: "agent-password")
  end

  test "only the owner, an admin, can cancel the account" do
    api_post("/account/cancel", token: @agent_token, account: "acme")

    assert_response :forbidden
    assert_equal "owner_only", json.dig("error", "code")
    assert_equal "active", Account.find_by!(subdomain: "acme").status_for_test
  end

  test "cancelling revokes every session and stops ordinary business access" do
    api_post("/account/cancel", token: @owner_token, account: "acme")

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "cancelled", json.dig("account", "status")
    assert json.dig("account", "cancelled_at").present?
    assert_equal json.dig("account", "cancelled_at").to_time + Account::REACTIVATION_WINDOW,
                 json.dig("account", "reactivation_deadline").to_time

    api_get("/me", token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :unauthorized

    api_get("/portal", account: "acme")
    assert_response :forbidden
    assert_equal "account_cancelled", json.dig("error", "code")
  end

  test "after cancelling, other users cannot sign in but the owner can, to reactivate" do
    api_post("/account/cancel", token: @owner_token, account: "acme")

    api_post("/sessions", { session: { email: "ann@acme.test", password: "agent-password" } }, account: "acme")
    assert_response :forbidden
    assert_equal "account_cancelled", json.dig("error", "code")

    owner_token = sign_in!(email: "jo@acme.test")

    api_get("/account", token: owner_token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "cancelled", json.dig("account", "status")

    api_get("/me", token: owner_token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :ok

    api_get("/portal", account: "acme")
    assert_response :forbidden
  end

  test "a cancelled account's sessions cannot reach ordinary endpoints" do
    api_post("/account/cancel", token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    owner_token = sign_in!(email: "jo@acme.test")

    api_patch("/me", { user: { name: "Changed" } }, token: owner_token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :ok

    # Account-level cancel is not something a cancelled account can repeat.
    api_post("/account/cancel", token: owner_token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :forbidden
  end

  test "the owner can reactivate within 90 days and then ordinary access resumes" do
    api_post("/account/cancel", token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    owner_token = sign_in!(email: "jo@acme.test")

    travel(89.days) do
      api_post("/account/reactivate", token: owner_token, account: "acme")
    end

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "active", json.dig("account", "status")
    assert_nil json.dig("account", "cancelled_at")

    api_get("/portal", account: "acme")
    assert_response :ok
    assert sign_in!(email: "ann@acme.test", password: "agent-password").present?
  end

  test "reactivation is refused after 90 days" do
    api_post("/account/cancel", token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    owner_token = sign_in!(email: "jo@acme.test")

    travel(Account::REACTIVATION_WINDOW + 1.minute) do
      api_post("/account/reactivate", token: owner_token, account: "acme")
    end

    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert_equal "reactivation_window_closed", json.dig("error", "code")
    assert Account.find_by!(subdomain: "acme").cancelled?
  end

  test "reactivating an account that is not cancelled is refused" do
    api_post("/account/reactivate", token: @owner_token, account: "acme")

    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert_equal "not_cancelled", json.dig("error", "code")
  end

  test "only the owner can reactivate" do
    api_post("/account/cancel", token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    api_post("/account/reactivate", token: @agent_token, account: "acme")

    assert_response :unauthorized
  end
end

class PurgeCancelledAccountsTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ApiHelpers

  setup do
    Rails.application.load_tasks unless Rake::Task.task_defined?("helpdesk:purge_cancelled_accounts")
    @old = create_account("old", cancelled_at: nil)
    @old.cancel!(now: 91.days.ago)
    @recent = create_account("recent")
    @recent.cancel!(now: 30.days.ago)
    @active = create_account("active")
  end

  test "purges accounts cancelled more than 90 days ago, with all their data" do
    old_user_id = @old.users.first.id
    old_session_user = @old.users.first
    Session.issue!(old_session_user)
    EmailVerification.issue!(old_session_user)
    PasswordReset.issue!(old_session_user)

    purged = Account.purge_cancelled!

    assert_equal 1, purged
    assert_nil Account.find_by(id: @old.id)
    assert_equal 0, User.where(account_id: @old.id).count
    assert_equal 0, User.where(id: old_user_id).count
    assert_equal 0, Session.where(user_id: old_user_id).count
    assert_equal 0, EmailVerification.where(user_id: old_user_id).count
    assert_equal 0, PasswordReset.where(user_id: old_user_id).count
  end

  test "keeps accounts still inside the reactivation window and active accounts" do
    Account.purge_cancelled!

    assert Account.exists?(@recent.id)
    assert Account.exists?(@active.id)
    assert @recent.reload.cancelled?
  end

  test "an account reactivated before the purge is kept" do
    @old.reactivate!

    assert_equal 0, Account.purge_cancelled!
    assert Account.exists?(@old.id)
  end

  test "the rake task performs the purge" do
    task = Rake::Task["helpdesk:purge_cancelled_accounts"]
    task.reenable

    assert_output(/Purged 1 cancelled account/) { task.invoke }
    assert_nil Account.find_by(id: @old.id)
    assert Account.exists?(@recent.id)
  end

  private

  def create_account(subdomain, cancelled_at: nil)
    account = Account.create!(name: subdomain.capitalize, subdomain: subdomain)
    admin = account.users.create!(
      name: "Owner", email: "owner@#{subdomain}.test", password: PASSWORD, role: "admin", verified_at: Time.current
    )
    admin.reload
    account
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class CorsTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  test "the configured frontend origin may call the API" do

      "Origin" => "http://localhost:3001",
      "Access-Control-Request-Method" => "POST",
      "Access-Control-Request-Headers" => "authorization,content-type,x-helpdesk-account"

  test "other origins are not allowed" do

      "Access-Control-Request-Method" => "POST"

  test "actual API responses carry the allow-origin header for the frontend" do
    get "/api/v1/portal", headers: { "Origin" => "http://localhost:3001", "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "nope" }

    assert_equal "http://localhost:3001", response.headers["access-control-allow-origin"]

end

messages.content:
Three failures. Two are test design problems and one is a real finding:

1. **Reactivation tests:** the owner's session was created *before* `travel(89.days)`. Sessions last 30 days, so it had expired by the time of the request. A real owner would sign in again, so the tests should do that inside the time-travel block.
2. **Missing envelope:** Rails' `wrap_parameters_by_default` (enabled by `load_defaults 8.1`) silently wrapped the bare JSON under `account`. That lets requests bypass the envelope the spec requires. I'll disable it so every endpoint uses explicit envelopes.

All 54 tests pass. Before I trust that, I'll check that the tests can actually fail: I'll deliberately break a few key rules and confirm the right tests catch each one.

But first, a robustness gap I noticed while reviewing the controllers. `params.require(:x)` returns a plain string if the client sends `{"x": "text"}`, and then `.permit` raises `NoMethodError`, which would be a 500 rather than a 400. I'll route envelope lookups through a helper that rejects non-objects. I'll also make the tests read the frontend URL and sender from `Helpdesk::Settings`, so they still pass if those environment variables are overridden.

arguments.command:
cd /app && python3 - <<'PY'
import re,glob
p='app/controllers/concerns/error_handling.rb'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''  private

  def render_error(''','''  private

  # Like params.require, but a value that is not an object (e.g. a bare string)
  # counts as missing, so the client gets a 400 instead of a server error.
  def require_params(key)
    value = params.require(key)
    raise ActionController::ParameterMissing, key unless value.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)

    value
  end

  def render_error(''')
open(p,'w').write(s)

for f in glob.glob('app/controllers/api/v1/*.rb'):
    s=open(f).read()
    s2=re.sub(r'params\.require\(', 'require_params(', s)
    if s2!=s:
        open(f,'w').write(s2)
        print("updated", f)
PY

    end
  end

    class EmailVerificationsController < ApplicationController
      GENERIC_MESSAGE = "If that email belongs to an account that needs verifying, a verification link is on its way.".freeze

      # Sends a fresh verification link. Replaces any earlier link.
      def create
        account = optional_account_from_header
        return if performed?

        email = require_params(:email_verification).permit(:email)[:email]
        scope = (account ? account.users : User.all).where(email: email, verified_at: nil)

        scope.includes(:account).each do |user|
          token = EmailVerification.issue!(user)
          UserMailer.deliver_safely(:email_verification, user, token)
        end

        render json: { message: GENERIC_MESSAGE }, status: :accepted
      end

      def confirm
        account = optional_account_from_header
        return if performed?

        token = require_params(:email_verification).permit(:token)[:token]
        user = nil

        EmailVerification.transaction do
          record = EmailVerification.redeem!(token, account: account)
          user = record.user
          user.verified_at ||= Time.current
          user.save!
        end

        render json: { message: "Email verified. You can sign in now.", user: user.as_api_json, account: user.account.as_api_json }
      rescue SingleUseToken::InvalidToken
        render_invalid_token
      end

      private

      def render_invalid_token
        render_error(:unprocessable_entity, "invalid_token", "This link is invalid or has expired. Request a new one.")
      end
    end
  end

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Helpdesk API

Rails API-only backend for a helpdesk SaaS. Businesses sign up, their owners verify
email and sign in, and each business has its own users. The frontend is a separate
app that talks to this API over JSON under `/api/v1`.

## Setup

Requires Ruby 4.0, PostgreSQL and the gems in the `Gemfile`.

```sh
bundle install
export DATABASE_URL=postgresql:///helpdesk_development?host=/var/lib/postgresql
bin/rails db:prepare          # creates and migrates the database
bin/rails server              # listens on PORT (default 3000)
bin/rails test                # runs the suite against a separate *_test database
```

Outgoing mail is written to `tmp/mails/` in development.

### Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | none (required) | PostgreSQL connection. |
| `TEST_DATABASE_URL` | `DATABASE_URL` with `_development` replaced by `_test` | Test database. Tests never use the development database. |
| `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL` | `http://localhost:3001` | Frontend base URL. Used for email links and as the only allowed CORS origin. |
| `HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM` | `support@example.test` | Sender address for all mail. |
| `SMTP_ADDRESS`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_DOMAIN`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | `localhost`, `587`, — | Production mail delivery. |

## Conventions

- Every request body uses an envelope, e.g. `{"session": {...}}`. Bare JSON is rejected.
- **Choosing a business:** send `X-Helpdesk-Account: <subdomain>`.
  - Signed-in requests can omit it. The token already identifies the business. If it is sent and does not match, the response is 403.
  - Sign-in, verification resend and password reset use it to find the user. Without it, the email must belong to exactly one business.
- **Signed-in requests:** send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- **Errors** share one shape: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "errors": {...}}}`. `errors` is present for validation failures. Validation keys are prefixed `account.` or `admin.` on signup.
- Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC.

## Endpoints

| Method and path | Auth | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/v1/account/create` | none | Sign up a business and its admin. Returns `201` with `account` and `user`. The admin is unverified and receives a verification email. |
| `GET /api/v1/portal` | header | Public `{"portal": {"name", "subdomain"}}`. |
| `POST /api/v1/sessions` | header optional | Sign in with `{"session": {"email", "password"}}`. Returns `201` with `session.token`, `user` and `account`. Unverified users get `403 email_not_verified`. |
| `DELETE /api/v1/session` | bearer | Sign out this session. `204`. |
| `GET /api/v1/me` / `PATCH /api/v1/me` | bearer | Profile. `PATCH` takes `{"user": {"name": "..."}}`. |
| `PUT /api/v1/me/password` | bearer | `{"password_change": {"current_password", "password"}}`. Signs out every session, including this one. |
| `POST /api/v1/email_verifications` | header optional | `{"email_verification": {"email"}}`. Sends a new link and replaces the old one. Returns `202`. |
| `POST /api/v1/email_verifications/confirm` | header optional | `{"email_verification": {"token"}}`. Marks the user verified. The token works once. |
| `POST /api/v1/password_resets` | header optional | `{"password_reset": {"email"}}`. Sends a new link and replaces the old one. Returns `202` whether or not the email exists. |
| `POST /api/v1/password_resets/confirm` | header optional | `{"password_reset": {"token", "password"}}`. Sets the password, signs out all sessions and verifies the email. The token works once. |
| `GET /api/v1/account` | bearer | Full account, including `status` and `reactivation_deadline`. |
| `POST /api/v1/account/cancel` | bearer, owner | Cancels the business and revokes all its sessions. |
| `POST /api/v1/account/reactivate` | bearer, owner | Reactivates a cancelled business within 90 days. |

Emailed links:

- `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL/verify-email?account=<subdomain>&token=<token>`
- `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL/reset-password?account=<subdomain>&token=<token>`

Token lifetimes are 3 days for verification and 2 hours for password reset. Sessions last 30 days.

## Accounts and roles

- The signing-up user is an `admin` and acts as the business owner. Only admins can cancel or reactivate.
- Other roles are `agent`. The API does not create them yet.
- Email addresses are unique within a business, so one email can belong to several businesses.
- Subdomains are unique across all businesses and must not be reserved (`www`, `api`, `app`, `admin`, ...).

### Cancellation

- `POST /account/cancel` sets `cancelled_at` and revokes every session in the business.
- While cancelled, only the owner can sign in. Ordinary access returns `403 account_cancelled`. The owner can still view the account, edit their profile, change their password, sign out, and reactivate.
- `POST /account/reactivate` works until 90 days after cancellation.
- Data is kept until the reactivation window closes.

### Permanent deletion

```sh
bin/rails helpdesk:purge_cancelled_accounts
```

This deletes every account cancelled more than 90 days ago, along with its users, sessions and tokens. Run it on a schedule, for example daily from cron. It is safe to run repeatedly.

## Layout

- `app/models/account.rb`: business, cancellation, reactivation window, purge.
- `app/models/user.rb`: users, roles, password rules.
- `app/models/session.rb`: bearer sessions (only token digests are stored).
- `app/models/concerns/single_use_token.rb`: replaceable, single-use tokens for verification and reset.
- `app/controllers/concerns/`: error format, business lookup from header, bearer auth and cancelled-account rules.
- `app/controllers/api/v1/`: endpoints.
- `app/mailers/user_mailer.rb`: verification and reset emails.
- `config/initializers/helpdesk.rb`: settings from the environment. `config/initializers/cors.rb`: frontend CORS.

    if body is not None: h["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    if token: h["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
